page: Microsoft Azure E32d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The configuration includes 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading, and 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU features 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 caches, alongside hardware flags such as AVX-512 for vector neural network instructions, AES, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions.

This server includes 1229 GB of local storage, providing high-speed local disk capacity directly bundled with the instance. In benchmark evaluations, the E32d_v5 demonstrates solid mid-range performance. Its stress-ng single-core CPU score is 1900.18, and the multi-core score reaches 31085.46. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1679.85 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write speeds reach 148.27 GB/sec and 68.94 GB/sec respectively. PassMark database operations benchmark at 15176.32, and Redis SET operations achieve 31.39 million operations per second.

For specialized workloads, the server supports single-threaded gzip compression at 28.52 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 71.19 GB/sec. Large language model inference benchmarks show strong text generation performance for small 135M models at 280.92 tokens/sec, though performance drops to a weak 6.65 tokens/sec for prompt processing on large 70B models, highlighting a tradeoff for massive AI workloads without dedicated GPU acceleration. Given its high resource density and bundled local storage, the E32d_v5 is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and software compilation.
